meta.title: ABT/BOS back-office — spec-grounded rewrite (Customers / Debt Recovery / Card Verification / Customer Services / Account Functions / Activity Log / Shift Board / Events & Alerts)

action_legend.grounded: Verified against a cited spec; kept, or tightened only for clarity/standard.
action_legend.rewrite: Substantive change to title/preface/steps to match the spec or the confirmed fact.
action_legend.unconfirmed: Feature is specified but not verified live — marked UNCONFIRMED, not asserted.

meta.citation_note: FBD .docx are cited by extractor paragraph number (extract_req.py). PSPEC PDFs are cited by document section (§) as the stable anchor — PDF text extraction puts each word on its own line so raw line numbers are unusable as citations. Task-supplied paras were re-verified: 'store… for historic reporting' is FBD-100307 para 367 (NOT 460 — para 460 is 'refunds not sent to MERIT'); FBD-100662 has no verbatim 'para 264 valid-only' statement in v5.00 — closest grounding is para 108 (Journey History built from device boarding/alighting stops). See changelog.
meta.no_invention: Every action/screen/field traces to a cited paragraph, or is marked GAP/UNCONFIRMED. Portal status labels, some UI button names, and print/cancel affordances that could not be confirmed in a spec are listed under gaps for the engineer Q&A loop, not asserted.

cases.title: Activity Log — filter by activity, device, and date/time
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can filter the Activity Log, that at least one of Activity or Device Type is required, and that a date/time range within the 7-day maximum is mandatory.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the CloudFare Activity Log is displayed with communicated device audit data
**AND** the results are scoped to devices whose home location is beneath the selected operating company

steps.content: **WHEN** the user applies a filter with neither Activity nor Device Type set, or with a date range greater than 7 continuous days
steps.expected:
**THEN** no results are returned
**AND** the mandatory-filter / >7-day condition is indicated (not an error)

steps.content: **WHEN** the user sets at least one of Activity or Device Type plus a date/time range of 7 days or fewer
steps.expected: **THEN** only the activities matching the selected filters are shown, chronologically

citations: FBD-100358 §Activity Log search rules (two primary filters, at least one mandatory; Date&Time always mandatory; 7-day max, >7 → warning, no results; out-of-estate device type → no results not error)
cases.change_note: Title tightened to standard. Added the two grounded validation rules the original omitted: (1) at-least-one-of Activity/Device-Type mandatory, (2) mandatory date/time range capped at 7 continuous days. Original asserted only a generic 'filter works'.
gaps: Screen label 'All Activities page' used by the original could not be confirmed against FBD-100358 (which names the module 'Activity Log'); confirm the exact live page/tab label.

cases.title: Activity Log — page through results
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can page through Activity Log results when there is more than one page.
cases.preconds: **GIVEN** the CloudFare Activity Log is displayed with more results than fit on one page

steps.content: **WHEN** the user navigates to the next and previous pages
steps.expected: **THEN** the adjacent pages of activities are shown

citations: FBD-100358 §Activity Log search rules (results are chronological, rows expand for detail); §Shift Viewer + export (page sizes 10/20/50/100)
cases.change_note: Kept. Title tightened to standard; behaviour unchanged and grounded.

cases.title: Activity Log — shows transactions, events and staff activity with detail
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that the Activity Log surfaces the full activity taxonomy — transactions, device-initiated events, and staff/shift activity — each expandable to its detail.
cases.preconds: **GIVEN** the CloudFare Activity Log is displayed with communicated device audit data covering transactions, events and staff shifts

steps.content: **WHEN** the user views the results and expands a Transaction, an Event, and a Start/End of Shift or Journey row
steps.expected:
**THEN** each activity type is listed with the standard summary fields (Device Type, Device ID, Operating Company, Activity, Date/Time, Fleet ID where applicable)
**AND** each row expands to its detail

citations: FBD-100358 §Activity types + sources (Transaction / Event / Annulment / Start-End Shift / Start-End Journey / …); §Activity Log search rules (standard summary fields, rows expand)
cases.change_note: Kept; grounded against the FBD-100358 activity taxonomy. Added the named summary fields and the expand-to-detail behaviour to make it executable.

cases.title: Activity Log — filter by barcode ID
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a user can filter the Activity Log by a barcode ID and see the barcode-validation activity for it.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** a HHD is commissioned and communicating with CloudFare
**AND** the Activity Log is displayed
**AND** multi-use barcode validations with a defined barcode ID exist in the range

steps.content: **WHEN** the user filters by a barcode ID
steps.expected: **THEN** only the Transaction/Annulment activities matching that barcode ID are shown

citations: FBD-100358 §Activity Log search rules (Barcode ID filter — Flowbird multi-use + mLink multi-use with a defined barcode ID only; Barcode ID applies to Transaction/Annulment)
FBD-100167 / FBD-100317 (multi-use vs single-use barcodes)
cases.change_note: Kept; grounded on the FBD-100358 Barcode ID filter. Softened the original's four states (validated/printed/failed/invalid) — see gaps.
gaps: FBD-100358 grounds a Barcode ID filter applicable to Transaction/Annulment, but does NOT enumerate 'validated / printed / failed / invalid barcode ID' as filter states — those four states are not in the cited spec. Confirm whether the live Activity Log exposes those specific barcode states, or whether they belong to a barcode report.

cases.title: Activity Log — failed validations, declined taps and failed payments are identified with reason
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that failed barcode validations, declined/invalid ABT taps and failed bank-card retail payments are visible in the Activity Log with their reason. This is the operator surface (with the reports and the stored audit) for reviewing invalid taps — declined/invalid taps do NOT appear as journeys in Journey History.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the CloudFare Activity Log is displayed with communicated device audit data
**AND** the data includes a failed barcode validation, an ABT tap declined at an ETM (e.g. Deny List / expired), and a failed bank-card retail payment

steps.content: **WHEN** the user reviews the failed barcode validation, the declined ABT tap and the failed bank-card retail payment
steps.expected:
**THEN** each failure is identified in the Activity Log with its reason
**AND** the declined ABT tap carries its Declined Reason (e.g. 2 = On Deny List, 1 = Card Expired)

citations: FBD-100358 §Activity types (Event = errors + transactions not in MERIT; failed validations shown)
FBD-100307 para 367 ('The device will store transaction information and declined reason for historic reporting'); para 222/376 (declined reason must be audited on Mode-2 failure)
FBD-100658 §Field rules (DeclinedReason enum: 0 Success / 1 Expired / 2 On Deny List / 3 Declined / 4 Cancelled / 15 On BIN List / 20 Passback)
cases.change_note: Strengthened to name the Declined Reason values and to state explicitly that this (with the Declined Taps report and the stored audit) is the surface for invalid taps — directly supports the C4102867 rewrite and the confirmed fact that Journey History shows valid journeys only.

**GIVEN** the Alert Viewer page is displayed under Events & Alerts with raised alerts
**AND** the signed-in user is a subscriber to those alerts

steps.content: **WHEN** the user filters by status (Acknowledged / Unacknowledged / Cleared / Uncleared) and severity

**AND** the alert can then be cleared

cases.change_note: Rewrote to encode the grounded ordering constraint (acknowledge-before-clear) the original missed, and the named status filters. Split acknowledge/clear into an ordered step.

cases.title: Debt Recovery — a recoverable debt is recovered and the card is re-enabled
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a recoverable debt is settled by the scheduled debt-recovery process and the linked cards are removed from the deny list and re-enabled in the Operator Portal.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card carries a recoverable debt (an EndOfDay authorisation that can be re-collected)
**AND** that card is linked on the same account to a second card, and both are currently blocked (on the deny list)
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content: **WHEN** you open the account and note the status of both linked cards
steps.expected: **THEN** both cards show a blocked / deny-listed status before recovery runs

steps.content: **WHEN** the scheduled debt-recovery process runs and re-collects the debt, and you refresh the account
steps.expected:
**THEN** both cards are removed from the deny list and re-enabled for travel
**AND** each card shows its expected number of authorisation requests

citations: FBD-100307 para 314-316 (debt recovery is the means for removing a card from the deny list; success → token removed, unsuccessful → remains)
FBD-100307 para 449 (automated re-auth also attempts to collect the original transaction value)
cases.change_note: Kept the scenario; re-expressed 'Blocked → Active' as the grounded 'removed from deny list / re-enabled for travel'. Flagged the portal status-label wording (see gaps) because it is inconsistent across cases and not confirmed in a spec.
gaps: Portal card-status labels are unverified and INCONSISTENT across the suite: this case uses 'Blocked'/'Active' while C4102854 uses 'ACCEPTED'. FBD-100307 speaks of deny-list membership and travel permitted/denied, not portal status strings. Confirm the exact live Operator-Portal status label(s) and standardise across C4102850/C4102851/C4102853/C4102854.
'Linked cards on the same account' (multiple cards per account both blocked/recovered together) is plausible but not confirmed in the cited specs — confirm the account/card linkage model.
'expected number of authorisation requests' — confirm where this count is shown in the portal.

cases.title: Debt Recovery — an unrecoverable debt leaves the cards blocked
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an unrecoverable debt leaves the linked cards on the deny list (blocked) in the Operator Portal after the recovery process runs.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card carries an unrecoverable debt (an authorisation that cannot be re-collected)
**AND** that card is linked on the same account to a second card, and both are currently blocked (on the deny list)
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content:
**WHEN** the scheduled debt-recovery process runs against the account
**AND** you refresh the account in the Operator Portal
steps.expected:
**THEN** both cards remain on the deny list (blocked)
**AND** each card shows its expected number of authorisation requests

citations: FBD-100307 para 316 ('If unsuccessful then the payment token will remain on the deny list')
cases.change_note: Kept; grounded. Re-expressed 'Blocked' as deny-list membership. Same status-label caveat as C4102850.
gaps: Portal status label 'Blocked' unverified (see C4102850 gaps).

cases.title: Debt Recovery — automated (scheme) recovery clears a recoverable issuer-liability debt
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that scheduled automated (card-scheme-driven) recovery clears a recoverable issuer-liability debt and removes the token from the deny list.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded test account has an EndOfDay authorisation failure and a recoverable debt within the issuer-liability threshold
**AND** the account is currently blocked and its token is on the ABT Deny List
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content:
**WHEN** the scheduled automated re-authorisation cycles run (per card-scheme rules) and re-collect the debt
**AND** you refresh the account in the Operator Portal
steps.expected:
**THEN** the account is no longer blocked in the Operator Portal
**AND** the account's token no longer appears on the Deny List

citations: FBD-100307 para 309 (Automated Debt Recovery Attempt: account on Deny List and card-scheme conditions reached to permit automated recovery)
FBD-100307 para 449 (automated re-auth attempts to collect the original transaction value)
PSPEC-0015 §4.7.3 Issuer Liability / Chargeback Protection
cases.change_note: Re-titled from 'Visa MIT recovery' to 'automated (scheme) recovery' — FBD-100307 defines the trigger as Automated Debt Recovery per card-scheme rules; 'Visa MIT (merchant-initiated)' is a scheme-implementation label not used in the cited spec. Kept the issuer-liability framing (PSPEC-0015 §4.7.3).
gaps: 'Visa MIT' terminology is not in FBD-100307 (which says 'automated debt recovery per scheme rules'). Confirm whether the test env specifically exercises the Visa MIT rail, or keep it scheme-agnostic.

cases.title: Debt Recovery — a successful recovery removes the card from the Deny List
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a successful debt recovery removes the card from the Deny List and re-enables it for travel.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card is on the Deny List with a recoverable debt
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content: **WHEN** you locate the card and confirm it appears on the Deny List
steps.expected: **THEN** the card is listed on the Deny List (not permitted for travel)

steps.content: **WHEN** the debt-recovery process runs, recovers the debt, and you refresh the account
steps.expected:
**THEN** the card is no longer on the Deny List
**AND** it is re-enabled for travel

citations: FBD-100307 para 316 (successful debt recovery → token removed from deny list)
FBD-100307 para 312-314 (a card on the deny list is not permitted for valid travel; debt recovery is the means of removal)
cases.change_note: Kept; grounded. Replaced 'status other than Active' / 'status Active' with the grounded deny-list membership + travel-enabled wording.

cases.title: Debt Recovery — the recovered account is visible in the Operator Portal with its correct status
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that, after a debt recovery completes, the account is findable on the Customers page by its masked PAN and shows the correct (recovered) status.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** a debt recovery has completed for the seeded ABT test card (masked PAN)
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal

steps.content: **WHEN** you open the Customers page and search for the card's masked PAN
steps.expected:
**THEN** the account record for that masked PAN is shown
**AND** it shows the correct recovered status (no longer on the deny list)

citations: FBD-100307 para 316 (token removed from deny list on successful recovery)
PSPEC-0015 §Customers / Account search (masked PAN)
cases.change_note: Removed the hard-coded status literal 'ACCEPTED' from the assertion because it CONFLICTS with C4102850/C4102853 which use 'Active' for the same recovered state. Re-expressed as 'correct recovered status (no longer on deny list)' pending the engineer confirming the one true label.
gaps: Status-label conflict: this case asserted 'ACCEPTED', C4102850/C4102853 assert 'Active' for the recovered state. Confirm the single correct live label and reconcile all four debt-recovery cases (POSSIBLE inconsistency introduced by copy-editing, not a spec fact).

cases.title: Debt Recovery — recovery outcome is verified in the portal; service logging by dev tests
cases.preface: This test documents the QA split: manual QA verifies the observable recovery outcome in the Operator Portal, while the open-payment-bs service logging is verified by automated dev tests (manual QA has no log access).
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** manual QA has no access to the open-payment-bs service logs
**AND** a debt recovery has completed for the seeded ABT test card
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content: **WHEN** you check the card's recovery outcome on the Customers page
steps.expected:
**THEN** the recovery is confirmed by the card being removed from the deny list and re-enabled for travel
**AND** the corresponding open-payment-bs log entries are confirmed separately by the automated dev tests, not this manual pack

citations: FBD-100307 para 314-316 (debt recovery removal is the observable outcome)
cases.change_note: Kept as a test-strategy/scope case (defines the manual-vs-dev-test boundary). Re-expressed the observable as deny-list removal rather than a status literal. This asserts a QA process, not a device behaviour — flagged so it is not mistaken for functional coverage.
gaps: This is a scope/strategy note rather than a behavioural test; consider whether it belongs in the suite or in test-plan documentation. 'open-payment-bs' is an internal service name — confirm the automated dev-test coverage actually exists.

cases.title: Deny List — a card is added when it fails payment authorisation at settlement
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a card whose payment fails authorisation at EndOfDay settlement is automatically added to the Deny List.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card is NOT on the Deny List
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content:
**WHEN** the card fails payment authorisation at EndOfDay settlement
**AND** you open the card on the Customers page and check the Deny List
steps.expected:
**THEN** the card's token has been added to the Deny List
**AND** the card is no longer permitted for valid travel

citations: FBD-100307 para 258 ('If the authorisation request is declined then the required details are added to the Deny List, so that additional travel is denied')
FBD-100307 para 42-43 (failed payments/pre-auth → cEMV media blocked; travel denied next use)
cases.change_note: Kept; grounded. Re-expressed 'status reflects the failed authorisation' as the grounded travel-denied consequence.

cases.title: Deny List — a listed card is declined at the validator and the tap is audited
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a card on the Deny List is declined at the validator (travel not permitted) and the declined tap is audited with the On-Deny-List reason.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card is on the Deny List
**AND** the target validator has pulled the latest Deny List delta file
**AND** the card is otherwise valid (not expired, supported scheme)

steps.content: **WHEN** the customer taps the deny-listed card at the validator
steps.expected:
**THEN** the tap is declined at the validator (travel not permitted)
**AND** the tap is audited with Declined Reason 2 (On Deny List)

citations: FBD-100307 para 312-314, para 42 (deny-listed card not permitted for travel; red light on ETM / driver error)
FBD-100658 §Field rules (DeclinedReason 2 = On Deny List)
FBD-100662 §Validation checks (Deny List → Declined Reason 2)
cases.change_note: Kept unchanged — already well grounded and standard-compliant (a model declined-tap audit case). Only tightened the title.

cases.title: Deny List — a card is removed and re-enabled when its debt is recovered via any trigger
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that a card is removed from the Deny List and re-enabled for travel when its debt is recovered through any of the recovery triggers.
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card is on the Deny List with an outstanding debt
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal on the Customers page

steps.content:
**WHEN** the debt is recovered via one of the three triggers — web-initiated (by the passenger OR an operator via a web portal), automated (per card-scheme rules), or tap-initiated (a tap by the already-denied card)
**AND** you refresh the card on the Customers page
steps.expected:
**THEN** the card is removed from the Deny List
**AND** the card is re-enabled for future travel

citations: FBD-100307 para 307-311 (three triggers: Web Initiated, Automated, Tap Initiated)
FBD-100307 para 305 ('Either the passenger themselves or an operator acting on behalf of the passenger can trigger a debt recovery via one of the web portals')
FBD-100307 para 439-442, 445-447 (re-authorisation triggers; success → removed from deny list)
cases.change_note: Re-aligned the original's 'four channels' to the spec's THREE triggers (web-initiated, automated, tap-initiated), noting that web-initiated covers both passenger and operator (para 305). The original's split of web into 'customer online' + 'operator online' is a UI-path distinction, not a fourth trigger — kept as a sub-note, not asserted as a distinct spec channel.

FBD-100342 §ABT composite claims (RefundApproval vs RefundAuthorisation — two-person control)

cases.title: Customer Services — operator reviews a customer's journeys over a date range
cases.preface: This test is to confirm that an operator can review a customer's journeys over a date range in Journey History (valid journeys only). Declined/invalid taps (expired, passback, deny list) do NOT appear as journeys here — they are reviewed via the Declined Taps report and the Activity Log failed-validations view, and are stored in the tap audit (DeclinedReason).
cases.preconds:
**GIVEN** a customer has performed both valid journeys and declined/invalid taps (e.g. an expired or deny-listed tap) on a payment card
**AND** the operator has selected the customer's card account in the Operator Portal

steps.content: **WHEN** the operator opens the customer's Journey History for a date range
steps.expected:
**THEN** the valid journeys in that range are shown (from device boarding/alighting stops)
**AND** the declined/invalid taps are NOT listed as journeys in this view

steps.content: **WHEN** the operator reviews the customer's declined/invalid taps via the Declined Taps report and the Activity Log failed-validations view
steps.expected: **THEN** each declined/invalid tap is visible there with its Declined Reason (e.g. 1 Expired, 2 On Deny List, 20 Passback)

citations: FBD-100662 para 108 (Journey History displays taps as journeys using device boarding/alighting stops — i.e. valid journeys)
FBD-100307 para 367 ('The device will store transaction information and declined reason for historic reporting'); para 222/376 (declined reason audited on failure)
FBD-100658 §Field rules (DeclinedReason enum 0/1/2/3/4/15/20 — audit data)
PSPEC-0015 §3.3.6 + REQ-3498.0 (see GAP — conflicting requirement that invalid taps be visible in the operator's customer-portal view)
cases.change_note: REWRITE per the confirmed fact and the task directive. Old title 'View all taps including taps not valid for a journey' asserted a portal 'all taps incl invalid' view that George confirms does not exist as a Journey-History surface. New case: operator reviews valid journeys over a date range (Journey History); the declined/invalid taps are reviewed via the Declined Taps report + Activity Log and stored in audit (DeclinedReason). NOTE: this is NOT invention on the original author's part — the old case traces to a real requirement (REQ-3498.0 / PSPEC-0015 §3.3.6) — which is exactly why the conflict below must be raised, not silently dropped.
gaps: **POSSIBLE SPEC / IMPLEMENTATION CONFLICT (raise in Q&A loop):** PSPEC-0015 §3.3.6 states verbatim 'All taps will be visible even if the taps are not valid for the journey i.e. operators must be able to see, in their view of the customer portal, all valid and invalid taps (i.e. expired, pass back, deny list, etc.) made by the customer', and REQ-3498.0 (TFTS Requirements Matrix) says the same ('As a Transport Operator I want all taps … to be visible even if the tap is not valid for a journey … i.e. Expired, passback, deny list'). This directly conflicts with the confirmed fact that Journey History shows valid journeys only and there is NO portal 'all taps incl invalid' view. Resolution options for the engineer: (a) REQ-3498 is satisfied by the Declined Taps report + Activity Log (the reframe above) — requirement met via a different surface; or (b) the operator customer-portal 'all taps incl invalid' view is genuinely missing → an unmet requirement / defect to raise. Needs George / product confirmation before this case is finalised.

Task-supplied citation 'FBD-100662 para 264' does not resolve to a verbatim 'valid journeys only' statement in FBD-100662 v5.00; closest grounding is para 108. Confirm the correct paragraph or accept para 108 as the anchor.
